[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (F) at (3.1,0);\coordinate (T) at (3.1,1.718);\draw (-0.35,0)--(O);\draw (O)--(F) node[midway,below] {$62\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (F)--(3.9,0);\draw (F)--(T) node[midway,right] {$h$};\draw (O)--(T);\coordinate (rqa) at ($(F)!0.25cm!(O)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(F)!0.25cm!(T)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(F)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$29^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=F--O--T};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The angle of elevation of the top of an apartment building from a point $62$ m from its base is $29^{\circ}$. Find the height $h$ of the building, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Divided $62$ by $\tan 29^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying, as if the height were in the denominator.
Used $\sin 29^{\circ}$ instead of $\tan 29^{\circ}$, treating $62$ m as the line-of-sight distance.
Used $\cos 29^{\circ}$ instead of $\tan 29^{\circ}$, pairing the height with the wrong ratio.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (A) at (0,2.38);\coordinate (C) at (0,0);\coordinate (Bp) at (3.529,0);\coordinate (Hz) at (4.379,2.38);\draw[dashed] (A)--(Hz);\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,left] {$85\text{ m}$};\draw (C)--(Bp) node[midway,below] {$d$};\draw (A)--(Bp);\coordinate (rqa) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(A)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(Bp)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(C)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$34^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=Bp--A--Hz};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
From the top of a lighthouse $85$ m above sea level, the angle of depression of a ship is $34^{\circ}$. Find the distance $d$ of the ship from the base of the lighthouse, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Multiplied $85$ by $\tan 34^{\circ}$ instead of dividing, as if the distance were opposite the angle.
Used $\sin 34^{\circ}$ instead of $\tan 34^{\circ}$, which gives the line-of-sight distance, not the horizontal distance.
Used $\cos 34^{\circ}$ instead of $\tan 34^{\circ}$, dividing the height by the wrong ratio.

questions.solution_text:
The angle of elevation of the lamp from the ship is also $34^{\circ}$, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\tan 34^{\circ}=\dfrac{85}{d}$
$d\tan 34^{\circ}=85$
$d=\dfrac{85}{\tan 34^{\circ}}$
$\approx 126\text{ m}$

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (F) at (3.96,0);\coordinate (T) at (3.96,1.65);\draw (-0.35,0)--(O);\draw (O)--(F) node[midway,below] {$3600\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (F)--(4.76,0);\draw (F)--(T) node[midway,right] {$1500\text{ m}$};\draw (O)--(T);\coordinate (rqa) at ($(F)!0.25cm!(O)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(F)!0.25cm!(T)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(F)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=1cm,angle eccentricity=1.3] {angle=F--O--T};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A plane is flying at an altitude of $1500$ m and is a horizontal distance of $3600$ m from an observer on the ground. Find the angle of elevation $\theta$ of the plane from the observer, to the nearest degree.

options.why: Swapped opposite and adjacent, computing $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3600}{1500}\right)$, which gives the angle at the plane.
Used $\sin^{-1}$, treating $3600$ m as the line-of-sight distance rather than the horizontal distance.
Used $\cos^{-1}$ of the same fraction, pairing the two given lengths with the wrong ratio.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (A) at (0,0.63);\coordinate (C) at (0,0);\coordinate (Bp) at (3.64,0);\coordinate (Hz) at (4.49,0.63);\draw[dashed] (A)--(Hz);\draw (A)--(C) node[midway,left] {$45\text{ m}$};\draw (C)--(Bp) node[midway,below] {$260\text{ m}$};\draw (A)--(Bp);\coordinate (rqa) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(A)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(C)!0.25cm!(Bp)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(C)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$\theta$",angle radius=1.1cm,angle eccentricity=1.3] {angle=Bp--A--Hz};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
From the top of a cliff $45$ m above sea level, a ship is $260$ m from the base of the cliff. Find the angle of depression $\theta$ of the ship from the top of the cliff, to the nearest degree.

options.why: Found the angle between the cliff face and the line of sight instead of the angle measured from the horizontal.
Truncated $9.8^{\circ}$ to $9^{\circ}$ instead of rounding to the nearest degree.

questions.solution_text:
The angle of elevation of the cliff top from the ship equals the angle of depression, alternate angles on parallel lines
$\tan\theta=\dfrac{45}{260}$
$\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{45}{260}\right)$
$\approx 10^{\circ}$

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\coordinate (F) at (2.416,0);\coordinate (T) at (2.416,2.1);\draw (-0.35,0)--(O);\draw (O)--(F);\draw[dashed] (F)--(3.216,0);\draw (F)--(T) node[midway,right] {$30\text{ m}$};\draw (O)--(T) node[midway,above left] {$L$};\coordinate (rqa) at ($(F)!0.25cm!(O)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(F)!0.25cm!(T)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(F)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$41^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=F--O--T};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The angle of elevation of the top of a $30$ m building from a point on the ground is $41^{\circ}$. Find the line-of-sight distance $L$ from that point to the top of the building, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Used $\tan 41^{\circ}$, which gives the horizontal distance along the ground rather than the line of sight.
Used $\cos 41^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 41^{\circ}$, pairing the height with the adjacent side.
Multiplied by $\sin 41^{\circ}$ instead of dividing, giving a line of sight shorter than the building.

A plane is flying at an altitude of $3000$ m. Its line-of-sight distance from an observer on the ground is $7500$ m. Find the angle of elevation $\theta$ of the plane from the observer, to the nearest degree.

options.why: Used $\tan^{-1}$, treating $7500$ m as the horizontal distance instead of the line-of-sight distance.
Used $\cos^{-1}$ of the same fraction, pairing the altitude with the adjacent side.

[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (G) at (0,0);\coordinate (Ey) at (0,0.33);\coordinate (Fb) at (2.64,0);\coordinate (Fe) at (2.64,0.33);\coordinate (Tp) at (2.64,3.262);\draw (G)--(Fb) node[midway,below] {$12\text{ m}$};\draw (G)--(Ey) node[midway,left] {$1.5\text{ m}$};\draw (Fb)--(Fe);\draw (Fe)--(Tp) node[midway,right] {$x$};\draw[dashed] (Ey)--(Fe);\draw (Ey)--(Tp);\coordinate (rqa) at ($(Fe)!0.25cm!(Ey)$);\coordinate (rqb) at ($(Fe)!0.25cm!(Tp)$);\draw (rqa)--($(rqa)+(rqb)-(Fe)$)--(rqb);\pic[draw,"$48^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=1.4] {angle=Fe--Ey--Tp};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Standing $12$ m from the base of a building, Noah measures the angle of elevation of the top of the building as $48^{\circ}$. His eyes are $1.5$ m above the ground. Find the height of the building, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Stopped at the height above eye level and forgot to add the $1.5$ m eye height.
Subtracted the $1.5$ m eye height instead of adding it.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan 48^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{12}$
$x=12\tan 48^{\circ}$
$=13.3273\ldots$
The height of the building is $x$ plus Noah's eye height.
$13.3273\ldots+1.5\approx 14.8\text{ m}$

[/tikz]
From the top of a cliff $70$ m above sea level, the angles of depression of two boats $B_1$ and $B_2$, in line with the base of the cliff, are $26^{\circ}$ and $39^{\circ}$. Find the distance between the two boats, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Added the two distances from the base of the cliff instead of subtracting them.
Gave the distance of the nearer boat from the base of the cliff rather than the gap between the boats.
Gave the distance of the further boat from the base of the cliff rather than the gap between the boats.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95]\coordinate (G) at (0,0);\coordinate (P) at (0,2.24);\coordinate (Mb) at (4.06,0);\coordinate (K) at (4.06,2.94);\coordinate (Hh) at (1.3,2.24);\coordinate (E) at (2.233,2.715);\draw (G)--(Mb) node[midway,below] {$2900\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (G)--(P) node[midway,left] {$1600\text{ m}$};\draw[dashed] (Mb)--(K) node[midway,right] {$2100\text{ m}$};\draw (3.06,0)--(K)--(5.06,0);\draw (Mb)--(5.06,0);\draw[dashed] (P)--(Hh);\draw[-{Stealth}] (P)--(E);\pic[draw,"$12^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.8cm,angle eccentricity=1.45] {angle=Hh--P--E};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A plane flying at an altitude of $1600$ m begins to climb at $12^{\circ}$ to the horizontal when the pilot sees a peak $2100$ m high, $2900$ m away horizontally. By how much will the plane clear the peak? Answer to the nearest metre.

options.why: Gave the height climbed over the $2900$ m without comparing the new altitude with the peak.
Gave $2100-1600$, the height the plane still had to climb, ignoring the climb calculation altogether.
Used $\sin 12^{\circ}$ instead of $\tan 12^{\circ}$, treating $2900$ m as the distance flown along the climb.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan 12^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{2900}$
$x=2900\tan 12^{\circ}$
$=616.41\ldots$
The plane is then at $1600+616.41\ldots=2216.41\ldots$ m.
$2216.41\ldots-2100\approx 116\text{ m}$

From the top of a building $54$ m tall, the angle between the vertical wall and the line of sight to a car is $71^{\circ}$. Find the distance $d$ of the car from the base of the building, to the nearest metre.

options.why: Multiplied $54$ by $\tan 19^{\circ}$ instead of dividing by it, after correctly finding the $19^{\circ}$ angle of depression.
Used $\sin 19^{\circ}$, which gives the line-of-sight distance rather than the horizontal distance.
Used $\cos 19^{\circ}$, dividing the height by the wrong ratio.
